summary: Iteration 44: verified the INR->USD currency rebase and the new organiser door-takings report end to end. Backend: 28 pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration44_usd_door.py (27 pass, 1 real defect). Frontend: Playwright runs as partner, member and admin covering the door-takings block (stat cards, row, empty state), currency switcher display conversion, checkout maths in USD/INR/AED, member orders, and admin money screens. PayPal orders were created only (never approved). All test data created (2 walk-in door sales, 1 TEST_AED event, test checkout orders, 1 TEST settlement) was deleted and participant_count restored - DB verified clean.

critical.issue: Header currency switcher is NOT display-only at checkout. Commerce.jsx sends `currency: <display currency>` to /api/checkout, and tax_for() derives the tax rate from the CHARGING currency's home country, so the USD amount actually charged changes with the display selection. Same event ($18.00): USD display -> GST 16% -> base total $20.88; INR display -> GST 18% -> $21.24; AED display -> VAT 5% -> $18.90. Reproduced on a smaller event: PayPal amount $7.08 (INR display) vs $6.96 (USD display). Requirement was USD base/charged with the switcher as display-only.

collected / commission_owed / commission_recovered are summed across rows that can each be in a different currency, then labelled with items[0]['currency']. Repro: one AED door sale (AED 25.50) + one USD door sale ($10.00) -> {"currency":"USD","collected":35.5,"commission_owed":10.65}, i.e. the card reads 'Collected at the door $35.50' when only ~$16.95 was taken. Convert each row to base USD before summing and keep the row currency for the table only.

minor.issue: An INR-display order is stamped gateway='razorpay_sim'; Razorpay has no live keys in preview, so the checkout page falls back to the test-mode simulate buttons / PayPal instead of the Stripe+PayPal path a USD order gets. Side effect of the same root cause as the HIGH issue above.

Returns 404 for a partner's draft event even for the owning organiser, so an organiser cannot preview an unpublished event via the public detail endpoint (worked around by using GET /api/partner/events in tests). Pre-existing, low impact.

ui_bugs.issue: When the only door sale is on an AED-priced event, the four stat cards read 'AED 25.50 / AED 7.65 / AED 0.00' directly under the $-denominated payout cards on the same screen - mixed symbols on one page. Root cause is the backend aggregate currency (see backend issue).
The 'Billed in {currency} - {x} equivalent' hint is hidden for INR (`!isINR` guard), so a member paying by PayPal from an INR cart is never shown the USD amount PayPal will charge.

React console error on every page: 'In HTML, <span> cannot be a child of <option>. This will cause a hydration error.' CurrencyPicker markup is clean, so another <select> renders a span inside its options.

integration_issues.issue: Switching the header currency changes the order's charging currency, tax jurisdiction and payment gateway, so it is not display-only as specified.

issues: Door-takings stat cards can show a different currency symbol (AED) than the payout cards ($) immediately above them

action_items: Make the header currency switcher truly display-only: send currency='USD' (base) to /api/checkout, or freeze tax to the member's country so the charged USD total does not change with the display selection.
Convert every door-takings row to base USD before summing collected/commission_owed/commission_recovered, and return the base currency in `currency` (keep row.currency for the table).
Show the 'Billed in USD - $x equivalent' hint for INR too (remove the !isINR guard) so PayPal payers see the real USD charge.
Fix the <span> inside <option> DOM-nesting React error.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py checkout(): tax_for(currency, ...) makes the tax rate a function of the charging currency, which is the mechanism by which a purely cosmetic currency switch alters the amount charged. Tax should follow the member/event jurisdiction, not the display currency.

server.py partner_door_takings(): aggregates float amounts from orders whose `currency` differs, then reports one currency - a money figure that can be materially wrong. Same anti-pattern exists in the admin KPI aggregates over historical INR orders.
server.py is 8,744 lines; the money/currency helpers (BASE_CURRENCY, fx_rates, price_event, checkout, paypal_usd) should be extracted into a pricing module.

success_rate.frontend: 90% (door-takings, currency display, admin money screens all pass; checkout currency semantics fail)

All removed; DB verified: 0 TEST orders/events/settlements, 0 door orders, participant_count restored.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iteration44_usd_door.py -n 0`; it self-cleans (test_cleanup at the end). The single expected failure is test_display_currency_switch_does_not_misscale_paypal, which encodes the display-currency/tax defect - it should pass once checkout stops taking the tax jurisdiction from the display currency. Use /app/backend/tests/door_seed44.py --seed / --clean to create or remove a UI-visible door sale. NOTE: cleanup deleted 51 pending orders for arjun.sethi@example.com (leftovers from this and earlier iterations); the member now has 0 pending orders, so any 'Retry payment' test needs a fresh checkout first. Historical INR orders/payments/settlements were left untouched as instructed and admin aggregates still sum them under the $ symbol (intentional).
rca_of_the_issue: Currency rebase itself is correct: settings.base_currency=USD, currencies table USD=1.0/INR=83.33/AED=3.67, plans $11.99/$23.99/$240.00, events/products/coupons USD-sized, organiser price_overrides preserved exactly (AED 200 checks out as charge_subtotal 200.00), PayPal amount == order USD charge_total. The remaining defect is that the display switcher is still wired into the checkout payload (Commerce.jsx `currency: cur`), and server-side tax_for() keys the tax rate off that charging currency, so a cosmetic switch changes both the tax percentage and the payment gateway - and therefore the USD amount PayPal charges. Independently, partner_door_takings sums multi-currency rows into one figure labelled with the first row's currency, overstating 'Collected at the door' whenever an organiser has door sales in more than one currency (this organiser has USD, AED, SGD and JPY events).
